title: Intake Workbench: Priority Decision Grid & Cutlist (Sprint 28)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the outcome of today's intake/workbench grooming session for Sprint 28. Goal: produce a pragmatic cutlist (ship / defer / park) and capture wireframe-level notes for top 6 items so engineering can start sizing and UX can iterate on mocks.

Scope & constraints:
- Scope limited to Console + routing/rollouts surfaces (non-enterprise backend changes are out unless they are strictly small infra flags).
- Sprint window: 2026-09-28 -> 2026-10-11 (2 weeks).
- Constraint: one mid-size UI epic (<= 40 pts) and up to three small stories (<= 8 pts each) unless we de-scope elsewhere.

Attendees:
- Priya Patel (product owner)
- Ethan Moore (PM, rollouts)
- Sofia Martinez (UX)
- Devon Kim (eng lead)
- Rashid Alvi (SRE)
- Notes/channel: #console-intake (Slack)

Methodology used:
- We applied a compact prioritization framework: Weighted Impact-Velocity (WIV) score.
  - Impact: customer reach * user impact (1-5).
  - Risk/Cost: combined effort & infra risk (1-5).
  - Velocity multiplier: likelihood of hitting sprint when scoped (0.5, 1.0, 1.3).
  - WIV = (Impact / Risk) * Velocity. Higher is better.
- Quick qualitative review for UX complexity and accessibility blockers.

Decision grid (axes):
- X-axis: Implementation Risk (Low -> High)
- Y-axis: User Value / Customer Impact (Low -> High)
- Quadrants map to: Ship-now (High value, Low risk), Plan-for-next (High value, High risk), Opportunistic (Low value, Low risk), Defer (Low value, High risk).

Prioritized cutlist (top items considered)
1) Route Edit: Inline metadata + validation (JIRA: RDW-3124)
   - Summary: Add inline editable metadata fields (name, tags, traffic weight) in the route detail header. Prevent invalid weights and warn about zero-traffic routes.
   - Estimated: 13 pts
   - WIV calculation: Impact 5 / Risk 2 * Velocity 1.0 = 2.5 -> Ship-now (recommended)
   - Acceptance criteria (AC):
     - Header shows editable name and tags; edits persist without full page reload.
     - Weight slider with validation preventing >100 total; show tooltip when changes would reduce active canary below threshold.
     - Unit tests for save flow + backend feature flag fallback.
   - UX notes: Keep compact, single-line tag chips, inline edit affordance (pencil icon), keyboard accessible.

2) Bulk Route Tagging + Filter (RDW-3199)
   - Summary: Multi-select routes and apply/remove tags, then filter by tags in the routes table.
   - Estimated: 8 pts (UI 5 + API 3)
   - WIV: Impact 4 / Risk 1 * Velocity 1.3 = 5.2 -> Ship-now
   - AC: Bulk selection preserves current filters; bulk action modal confirms changes and shows sample preview row.
   - Wireframe notes: Add top-bar action group (Tag, Export, Delete), bulk state persists during pagination.

3) Intake Form: Priority Reason & SLA field (RDW-3256)
   - Summary: Add structured "Priority Reason" with short canned options + free text; capture requested SLO target for triage.
   - Estimated: 5 pts
   - WIV: Impact 3 / Risk 1 * Velocity 1.0 = 3.0 -> Plan-for-next (do if capacity)
   - Notes: Needs small backend storage change (one new enum + optional string).

4) Route Rollout Visual Timeline (RDW-3205)
   - Summary: Visual timeline for canary stages per route, with hover to reveal metrics snapshot.
   - Estimated: 21 pts (large front-end work + metrics integration)
   - WIV: Impact 5 / Risk 4 * Velocity 0.5 = 0.625 -> Plan-for-next (defer this sprint)
   - Rationale: high customer value but high front-end/metrics coupling. Break into epics later.

5) Quick Switcher: Jump-to-route (RDW-3183)
   - Summary: Cmd/Ctrl-K quick switcher to open routes by name or id.
   - Estimated: 3 pts
   - WIV: Impact 2 / Risk 1 * Velocity 1.3 = 2.6 -> Opportunistic (if we have cycles)

6) Audit trail compact view (RDW-3210)
   - Summary: Add condensed audit row in routes list showing last change actor and time.
   - Estimated: 5 pts
   - WIV: Impact 2 / Risk 2 * Velocity 1.0 = 1.0 -> Defer (low ROI vs other items)

Cut decisions (final):
- Ship this sprint: RDW-3124 (Route Edit inline) and RDW-3199 (Bulk Tagging).
- Park / Plan: RDW-3205 (Rollout Timeline) - break into two smaller spikes (ui mock + metrics contract).
- Opportunistic: RDW-3183 (Quick Switcher) if team capacity after finishing ship items.
- Defer: RDW-3210 (Audit compact) until next grooming.

Wireframe / UX writeups (top 2 ship items)
A) Route Edit: Inline metadata + validation (RDW-3124)
- Canvas: route detail header with three compact fields (name, tag chips, weight slider). Save is inline (30ms optimistic UI).
- States to design: initial read-only, hover -> edit affordance, editing -> inline save / cancel, saving -> success toast / error handling.
- Edge cases: concurrent edits (two users) -> show "stale" notice; precision when many routes weight rebalances are needed.
- Accessibility: inputs reachable via tab, slider with visible focus ring, tags readable by screen reader.
- Prototype link: (Sofia will push sketches by 2026-09-18)

B) Bulk Route Tagging (RDW-3199)
- Table behavior: checkboxes in first column, multi-select toolbar pinned at top.
- Bulk modal: shows tag suggestions based on selected routes' existing tags (top 3). Option to preview sample of up to 3 rows.
- Undo: on success, show undo toast valid for 8s that reverses last bulk operation.

Engineering notes & constraints:
- Backend: small API endpoints already planned (RDW-TRACK-API) for batch tag mutation; engage infra for rate limit checks (Rashid).
- Feature flag: route-inline-edit.v1 toggled on a per-org basis to allow quick rollback.
- Telemetry: track events: route_edit_start, route_edit_save, bulk_tag_apply, bulk_tag_undo. Add tags for success/failure codes.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we enforce tag taxonomy? (proposal: soft suggestions, not enforced for initial roll) -> assigned to Priya to decide by 9/17.
- Weight validation UX: what happens if saving new weights would violate another constraint (quota)? Quick decision: show blocking modal with exact reason and suggested remap. Devon to spike API behavior.

Action items (owners):
- Sofia: create hi-fi mockups for Route Edit + Bulk Tagging by 2026-09-18 (collab with Ethan).
- Devon: tech spike for concurrent edit handling and weight validation path by 2026-09-20.
- Ethan: update acceptance criteria in RDW-3124 and post notes to Jira ticket.
- Rashid: review rate-limit implications for bulk tag API by 2026-09-19.

Notes to reviewers:
- This cutlist intentionally favors low-risk high-impact work to preserve velocity while delivering immediate UX wins for power users. If engineering capacity opens, we can pull Quick Switcher next; timeline for rollout timeline is Q4 spike.

Appendix: Quick mock checklist (for UX handoff)
- Break components into: header-edit, editable tag chip, weight-slider, bulk-toolbar, bulk-modal.
- Provide keyboard flow and aria labels for each component.
- Document storybook stories for each piece (Sofia to add knobs).

Slack reference: thread pinned in #console-intake titled "intake workbench grooming 2026-09-15".

End of doc.
